title: Publications tracker (90-161.Z): seven questions for the commander

slides.title: Publications tracker (90-161.Z): seven questions
slides.subtitle:
For the commander and group commanders
Draft r5 · 12 November 2026 · about 10 minutes
slides.notes: Wing-internal brief. Each slide asks one question. No government data is in this brief.

slides.title: How this brief works
facts: Each slide asks one question.
Answer each one Yes, No or Pending evaluation.
The last slide is an answer sheet.
Recommendations are marked; they are the PFM's advice, not decisions.

slides.title: 1. Should the wing track its publications in one tool?
facts: Today, status sits in e-mail and spreadsheets.
The tool shows every publication's status in one place.
It follows the Air Force publishing manual (DAFMAN 90-161).
choices: Keep building it for our wing.
Decide after the pilot with test data.
slides.notes: Why use it. It replaces the wing checklist, action officer guide, template and workbook (PFM decision, 11 Nov).

slides.title: 2. Is it far enough along to pilot with test data?
facts: Data lists: working (tested 11 Nov).
Document formatter: nearly; 2 small fixes left.
Reminders and the app: not built yet.
choices: Finish the build; pilot with test data.
Wait for the access test results.
slides.notes: Does it work. All tests so far used fake data only.

slides.title: 3. If it breaks, is the backup plan good enough?
facts: Work continues by hand, as it does today.
No data is lost: every change is kept.
A backup person takes over with written steps.
slides.notes: What happens if it breaks. Deleted items can be restored for 93 days; a regular export is planned.

slides.title: 4. Do you accept the cost?
facts: $0 in new licenses expected; the license manager confirms.
The PFM's time to build: already under way.
A backup person: a few hours to learn it.
choices: Wait for the license manager's answer.
slides.notes: Cost. The design uses standard DoD365 tools only and forbids paid add-ons.

slides.title: 5. Should five offices review it before real use?
facts: It is not approved for use yet.
Reviews: cyber security (ISSM), Public Affairs and OPSEC, legal (SJA), privacy, records.
Nothing real goes into the tool before their answers.
choices: Task them after the test-data pilot.
slides.notes: Is it approved for use. Not yet.

slides.title: 6. Will you name a backup person?
facts: Today one person builds and runs it.
If that person leaves, the reminders stop.
A backup needs a few hours to learn it.

slides.title: 7. Do you accept the top two risks with these fixes?
facts: Design files are public: Public Affairs and OPSEC review them.
Some features need access we may not have: we test it first; each has a fallback.
choices: Stop until the risks are closed.
slides.notes: Risks R01 and R30 in the risk register.

slides.title: Answer sheet
rows: Track the wing's publications in one tool?
Five offices review it before real use?
Accept the top three risks with these fixes?
slides.note: Recommended: Yes on all seven. Pending evaluation keeps that part on hold; the PFM reports back.
